items.readable_text:
Content:
The additive properties of integrals are beneficial when we have to integrate a piecewise function, such as
[MATH: {x,|x < 0; 5,|x ≥ 0.]

Content:
For example, let's calculate the integral
[MATH: \displaystyle \int_{-5}^4 f(x) \,\textrm{d}x.]

Content:
We can split the integral into two integrals using the additive property, one integral for each "piece" of the piecewise function.

Content:
- The first integral will be over the integral [MATH: [-5,0],] and
- the second integral will be over the integral [MATH: [0,4].]

Content:
Doing this, we get the following:
[MATH: ∫_{− 5}^{4}f(x)dx|= ∫_{− 5}^{0}f(x)dx + ∫_{0}^{4}f(x)dx; = ∫_{− 5}^{0}xdx + ∫_{0}^{4}5dx; = (1)/(2)x^{2}|_{− 5}^{0} + 5x|_{0}^{4}; = (1)/(2)[0^{2} − (− 5)^{2}] + 5[4 − 0]; = − (25)/(2) + 20; = (15)/(2)]

[MATH: ∫_{− 2}^{5}f(x)dx|= ∫_{− 2}^{0}3dx + ∫_{0}^{5}(2x + 3)dx; = 3x|_{− 2}^{0} + (x^{2} + 3x)|_{0}^{5}; = [3(0) − 3(− 2)] + [(5^{2} + 3(5)) − (0^{2} + 3(0))]; = 6 + 25 + 15; = 46.]

The graph of [MATH: y=f(x),] shown above, consists of two line segments. Find the value of [MATH: \displaystyle \int_{0}^{4} f(x)\: \textrm{d}x.]

sections.normalized_html:
The graph consists of two parts: the line segment for [MATH: x \in [0,2)] and the line segment for [MATH: x \in [2,4].] Therefore, we can write the required integral as follows: [MATH: \int_{0}^{4} f(x)\: \textrm{d}x = \underbrace{\int_{0}^{2} f(x)\: \textrm{d}x}_{A_1} + \underbrace{\int_{2}^{4} f(x)\: \textrm{d}x}_{-A_2}.]

  • The [MATH: 1]st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the [MATH: x]-axis, where [MATH: x \in [0,2).] The corresponding region is a rectangle, so we find the area using the formula [MATH: A_{1}|= bh; = 2 ⋅ 2; = 4.]

  • The [MATH: 2]nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the [MATH: x]-axis, where [MATH: x \in [2,4].] The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula [MATH: A_{2}|= (1)/(2)bh; = (1)/(2) ⋅ 2 ⋅ 2; = 2.] Since the region lies below the [MATH: x]-axis, we have [MATH: \int_{2}^{4} f(x)\: \textrm{d}x =-A_2 = -2.]

Finally, we obtain [MATH: ∫_{1}^{4}f(x)dx|= A_{1} − A_{2}; = 4 − 2; = 2.]

  • The [MATH: 3]rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the [MATH: x]-axis, where [MATH: x \in (2,4].] The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula [MATH: A_{3}|= (1)/(2)bh; = (1)/(2) ⋅ 2 ⋅ 2; = 2.]

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

[MATH: {x,|x < 0; 5,|x ≥ 0.]

[MATH: \displaystyle \int_{-5}^4 f(x) \,\textrm{d}x.]

Content:
We can split the integral into two integrals using the additive property, one integral for each "piece" of the piecewise function.

Content:
- The first integral will be over the integral [MATH: [-5,0],] and
- the second integral will be over the integral [MATH: [0,4].]

Doing this, we get the following:
[MATH: ∫_{− 5}^{4}f(x)dx|= ∫_{− 5}^{0}f(x)dx + ∫_{0}^{4}f(x)dx; = ∫_{− 5}^{0}xdx + ∫_{0}^{4}5dx; = (1)/(2)x^{2}|_{− 5}^{0} + 5x|_{0}^{4}; = (1)/(2)[0^{2} − (− 5)^{2}] + 5[4 − 0]; = − (25)/(2) + 20; = (15)/(2)]

[MATH: ∫_{− 4}^{4}f(x)dx|= ∫_{− 4}^{0}f(x)dx + ∫_{0}^{2}f(x)dx + ∫_{2}^{2}f(x)dx + ∫_{2}^{4}f(x)dx; = ∫_{− 4}^{0}f(x)dx_(⏟)_(A_{1}) + ∫_{0}^{2}f(x)dx_(⏟)_(− A_{2}) + 0 + ∫_{2}^{4}f(x)dx_(⏟)_(A_{3}).]
